title: Dynamic SLO watermarking and regional quarantine adapter
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: intermittent regional surges from a small set of tenants were causing sustained SLO violations despite existing static throttles. This PR introduces a runtime watermarking mechanism that computes per-tenant SLO watermarks from latency and token-usage histograms and a regional quarantine adapter that places manic tenants into a short probationary quarantine with progressive re-admit logic. The change is opt-in via feature flags and is compatible with existing admission and circuit-breaker flows. Key behaviors: dynamic watermarking emits a moving SLO threshold per tenant based on p50/p95 latency trends and recent KV-pressure; the quarantine adapter signals routing to standby pools and applies an exponential backoff for re-admit windows; telemetry emits watermark_offset, quarantine_state, and quarantine_retries metrics; rollout is staged with a canary and gradual ramp controlled by the feature flag. Implementation notes: watermark manager is a lightweight in-memory controller with a pluggable policy interface, quarantine adapter hooks into the scheduler admission path and defers to existing fallback policies when capacity is limited. Testing: unit tests for watermark computation and adapter decision logic, integration e2e that simulates tenant surge and validates graceful tenant re-admit. Docs and ops runbook added. Related Linear: ENG-3291.

release_notes: Introduce dynamic SLO watermarking and a regional quarantine adapter to improve graceful degradation during tenant surges. Opt-in via feature flag 'dynamic_slo_watermarking'. Emitted metrics: watermark_offset, quarantine_state, quarantine_retries. Rollout requires a staged canary and monitoring of p50/p95 and KV pressure.
testing_notes: Unit coverage added for watermark math and adapter decision tree. Integration e2e simulates 100 tenants with synthetic latency spikes and validates that quarantined tenants are routed to standby pools and re-admit windows follow exponential backoff. CI initially surfaced a timing flake which was fixed by making e2e event-driven.
rollout_plan: Step 1: merge to main behind feature flag off. Step 2: enable feature flag in canary cluster for 5% of traffic for 24 hours while monitoring watermark_offset and quarantine_state metrics. Step 3: incrementally ramp to 25% then 100% if no regressions. Step 4: emergency rollback path via feature flag toggle or configmap revert. Ops runbook included in docs/operations/slo-watermarking.md.
motivation: Static limits caused expensive false positives during benign spikes; dynamic watermarks let the system adapt based on observed latency distributions and resource pressure, reducing unnecessary evictions while protecting SLOs.
notes_for_oncall: If quarantine_state count for a region rises suddenly, consider pausing ramp and investigate tenant-level traffic patterns. Use the quarantine_region tag to scope dashboards. In emergency, toggle dynamic_slo_watermarking to false and run configmap rollback.
